# Menu — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a menu when a set of actions belongs to one thing and showing them all would crowd it: a row's overflow, a file's options, an editor's insert menu. The menu is about doing — every entry acts and closes. If an entry goes somewhere instead, that is a navigation menu; if it picks a value, that is a select. Group related entries and label the groups, because a flat list of twelve verbs is a memory test. Destructive entries belong at the bottom, away from the ones people mean to press.

### Usage

**Do**

- Anchor to the trigger with a relative parent; the menu positions to it.
- Keep items to one line with an optional supporting line — dense rows use the menu-item height role.
- Separate groups with dividers (separator role, never focusable).

**Don't**

- Don't nest deeper than one submenu — flatten instead.
- Don't hide disabled items — show them inert so the set reads complete.

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| MenuRoot | Owns the open state for one menu. |
| MenuTrigger | The control the menu belongs to. Carries the expanded state. |
| MenuContent | The list surface. Portals to the end of the document and positions itself against its trigger. |
| MenuItem | One action. Activating it runs it and closes the menu. |
| MenuSeparator | A divider between runs of related actions. |
| MenuGroupLabel | Names a run of related actions, so the list reads as sections rather than a flat column. |
| Menu | The namespace object: all of the parts above. |

### FAQ

**Menu, select, or combobox?**

Menu for command lists from a trigger; select for fixed-value form fields; combobox for filter-as-you-type.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a menu when a trigger should offer a few actions without taking the reader anywhere: an overflow list, a set of options on an item, an edit menu. The trigger is yours — you pass the content and you pass its NAME, because `triggerLabel` is required rather than inferred. The items are data, and note the callback is `onSelect`, not `onPress`: the grouped menu family (`MenuGroupList`, `MenuScreen`, `MenuSheet`) calls the same thing `onPress`, so copying an action between the two forms needs that one rename. Keep the list short and the actions reversible; a menu with many choices or destructive ones wants a different surface.

### Usage

**Do**

- Declare items as data — `label`, optional `onSelect`, optional `disabled` — so the list renders identically wherever it opens.
- Keep the item count short enough to scan; a menu is a choice, not a catalog.
- Disabled items stay visible and inert rather than vanishing, so the set reads as stable.

**Don't**

- Don't nest menus — one level is the whole pattern.
- Don't put the only path to a destination inside a menu without a visible trigger that names it.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Surface | resting | theme.color.surfaceContainer | surfaceContainer, minWidth 112 |
| Surface shape | resting | theme.shape.small | small corners |
| Item | resting | theme.color.onSurface | onSurface label, minHeight 48 |

### FAQ

**Menu or action sheet?**

A menu hangs off its trigger where it stands; an action sheet rises as its own surface with a fixed action row. Trigger-anchored choice means menu.

**How does this differ from the web menu?**

The contract is the same (items as data, disabled stays visible). The surface is a native modal with a scrim rather than a positioned popup, and the trigger is a slot you own.
